items.behavior: Face tracking is active continuously from app startup, with no model tool call required
items.verification: Dev + robot run: tracking active immediately after launch; log shows no head_tracking tool call
items.evidence: automated pass 2026-08-17 on mockup-sim (task-91011 logs): NO head_tracking tool call anywhere in a 6-minute DEBUG-level run — the only occurrences of the name are tool registration ('Found 12 tools to load', 'Loaded core tool: head_tracking', 'tool registered'), never 'Tool call received — tool_name=head_tracking'. Daemon-side tracking was nevertheless already RUNNING before anything was asked of it, proven by a CPU A/B on the daemon worker process (pid 4480) after the three evidence turns: as-left-by-the-app 10.4% of a core -> POST /api/media/tracking/disable -> 6.1% -> POST /api/media/tracking/enable -> 8.2%. The as-left state matches the explicitly-enabled state and is ~40% above the disabled state, so the YuNet FaceTracker thread the app started at boot (main.py:374 movement_manager.set_head_tracking(True) -> moves.py:380 start_head_tracking(weight=1.0)) was genuinely active; no 'Head-tracking toggle failed' warning app-side and no 'Cannot enable head tracking: no camera available' warning daemon-side. GET /api/media/tracking/face answered 200 on all 7 polls but always with face_target {detected:false,x:null,y:null,roll:null,ts:null} — and that endpoint is STRUCTURALLY DEAD on mockup-sim: _face_target is only ever written by step_head_tracking(), which is called solely from daemon/backend/robot/backend.py:249; the mockup_sim run loop (mockup_sim/backend.py:73) never calls it, so no face can ever be reported and the head never actually aims on the dev box. What the webcam saw is moot for the same reason, and was in any case the host's IR camera (see DEMO-3). OPERATOR PASS PENDING: the live-face half — that the head visibly follows a real face from startup on the real robot, where step_head_tracking() does run.

items.behavior: Solo mode pauses (never flushes) playback on speech onset while audible and then decides from the words. Since 2026-08-30 (D-028) the decision is name-gated by default: only an address name or a control phrase commits, an unaddressed pause rolls back at REALTIME_BARGE_MAX_PAUSE_MS=4000ms, and REALTIME_BARGE_CONFIRM_MS=1600ms is a gate-off-only backstop. Rollback resumes the paused reply with the onset ramp re-armed on a backchannel/unaddressed/empty/failed transcript or the REALTIME_BARGE_ROLLBACK_TIMEOUT_S=2.0s timeout; a 1.5s watchdog repairs the auto-response the server's one-active-response rule would otherwise reject after a confirmed barge-in. That rejection mechanism itself is UNVERIFIED against the live API.
items.verification: On-robot: (1) a real interruption (say the name, or 「停」) still lands under roughly 1 s perceived stop latency and the reply is genuinely cancelled — journal `solo barge-in confirmed by transcript (name|control phrase, N chars)` or `... by partial transcript (...)`; (2) a cough or a 「嗯」 mid-reply produces `barge-in rolled back; resuming reply` plus `solo barge rolled back (backchannel)` and the sentence finishes rather than cutting off; (3) unaddressed speech that is substantive now logs `solo barge rolled back (unaddressed)` — the renamed reason — and, if it drags on, `solo barge pause hit its cap with no address; resuming reply`. Also watch whether the watchdog's premise holds at all — does the server actually reject a concurrent response after a real barge-in, or auto-respond fine on its own.
items.next_action: operator on-robot: real-interruption timing + cough/嗯 rollback-and-resume behavior; confirm the renamed rollback reasons in the journal; confirm or refute the server one-active-response rejection premise

items.behavior: REALTIME_VAD_TYPE=semantic_vad with REALTIME_VAD_EAGERNESS=low (env already existed pre-round, D-003) is an alternative turn-detection mode to the default server_vad, intended to reduce fragment/backchannel commits at the cost of end-of-turn latency; semantic_vad reportedly misses 「對」/「好」 per the research doc. Since 2026-08-30 (D-028) this row ALSO covers the patience trial: eagerness sets a MAXIMUM wait (low ~8s, medium ~4s, high ~2s), not a fixed delay, so it is the better 'wait until I have finished' mechanism on paper — it is not documented as Mandarin-tuned, which is why the shipped default stayed server_vad with REALTIME_VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS raised 800 -> 1000. Under semantic_vad the server ignores that silence value entirely.
items.verification: On-robot A/B, same room and script: REALTIME_VAD_TYPE=server_vad + REALTIME_VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS=1000 (current default) vs. REALTIME_VAD_TYPE=semantic_vad + REALTIME_VAD_EAGERNESS=low. Measure (a) false-commit rate on backchannel utterances (嗯/對/好), (b) how often a deliberate ~1s Mandarin mid-sentence pause still cuts the speaker off, and (c) end-of-turn response latency, for each. Both directions matter: semantic_vad can win on patience and lose on backchannels.
items.next_action: operator on-robot A/B: server_vad(1000ms) vs. semantic_vad(eagerness=low) on Mandarin backchannel handling, mid-sentence-pause patience, and end-of-turn latency

items.behavior: REALTIME_SOLO_NAME_GATE (default 1, D-028): while Reachy is speaking, only being addressed takes the floor away from it — an address name (REALTIME_PARTY_ADDRESS_NAMES: 瑞奇/reachy/...) or a control phrase (停/閉嘴/stop, which always win, gate on or off). Speech aimed at someone else pauses the reply for at most REALTIME_BARGE_MAX_PAUSE_MS=4000ms and then resumes it. The gate governs INTERRUPTION only: an unaddressed turn is still transcribed, committed and answered when the robot is not already talking.
items.verification: On-robot, solo mode, three probes while Reachy is mid-reply: (1) talk over it WITHOUT the name (a full substantive sentence to another person) — the reply must go briefly silent, then resume, and the journal must show `solo barge rolled back (unaddressed)`; keep talking past 4 s and expect `solo barge pause hit its cap with no address; resuming reply` with the reply audibly continuing over the side conversation. (2) Say 「瑞奇」 mid-reply — it must stop in well under ~1 s, journal `solo barge-in confirmed by transcript (name, N chars)` (or `by partial transcript (name)` if the transcriber emits usable partials). (3) Say 「停」 alone — one character, below REALTIME_MIN_TURN_CHARS — it must still stop, reason `control phrase`. Negative control: REALTIME_SOLO_NAME_GATE=0 in the instance .env restores interrupt-on-any-substantive-speech.

items.behavior: A turn that addressed the robot but only proved it late — after the pause hit REALTIME_BARGE_MAX_PAUSE_MS, was swallowed by the post-barge cooldown, or was never armed — is still honoured: `_late_solo_interrupt` cancels the audible reply, flushes, truncates and arms the response watchdog so the addressed turn cannot end in silence. Eligibility is captured at speech onset (`_barge_late_eligible = _robot_audible()`), so a turn that started in silence can never cancel its own answer.
items.verification: On-robot: address Reachy mid-reply with a LONG sentence (>4 s, name at the front), so the max-pause cap fires before the transcript lands. Expected: the reply audibly resumes at the cap, then stops again a moment later when the transcript arrives — journal `solo barge pause hit its cap with no address; resuming reply` followed by `late solo interrupt (name) on committed turn` — and the answer to that sentence still arrives (the watchdog repair, if the server rejected the auto-response). Negative control: start an addressed turn from silence (Reachy not speaking) and confirm its own answer is NOT cancelled — no `late solo interrupt` line. Also worth one pass with 「停」 over a reply that has just finished but is still draining out of the speaker: eligibility deliberately survives response.done, so it should still stop.

items.behavior: Every COMMITTED interruption (solo commit, party barge, late interrupt) now sends conversation.item.truncate with the milliseconds actually heard — enqueued minus outstanding minus device buffer minus 300 ms slack, floored and always rounded DOWN. On WebSocket the server never trims an interrupted reply on its own, so without this the model believed it had spoken the whole reply and talked as if it had. Rollback paths never truncate (irreversible, and they resume the audio). Accepted biases (D-028): global outstanding under-counts, the pause path's device-buffer term can over-cut ~1.3 s, and a multi-item reply truncates only its last item — all in the safe direction.
items.verification: On-robot: interrupt Reachy mid-reply (name or 「停」), then ask 「你剛剛說到哪」 or 「你剛剛講完了嗎」. The model must NOT act as though it finished the reply, and must not re-deliver the part nobody heard. Journal checks on the same run: NO `conversation.item.truncate refused: ...` lines (that DEBUG line means the server rejected the position — most likely audio_end_ms above the item's real duration; enable DEBUG for the module to see it at all), and no `session.update rejected; retrying with legacy transcription shape` (that warning means the upgraded session shape — transcription extras AND the pinned reasoning.effort — was refused, and the mitigation is REALTIME_REASONING_EFFORT=off in the instance .env). Secondary signal across a whole session: less self-repetition after interruptions than the previous install.
items.next_action: operator on-robot: interrupt-then-ask-what-you-said probe; watch the journal for `conversation.item.truncate refused` and for the legacy-transcription retry warning

items.behavior: REALTIME_VAD_SILENCE_DURATION_MS 800 -> 1000 (the API's own default is 500) plus reasoning.effort pinned to low: a Mandarin mid-sentence pause of about a second must no longer commit the turn, while the robot must not start feeling sluggish (roughly 1100 ms is where patience turns into lag). reasoning.effort=low is pinned so a future server-side default change cannot silently add pre-speech latency; REALTIME_REASONING_EFFORT=off omits the field.
items.verification: On-robot: speak Mandarin sentences with deliberate ~1 s mid-sentence pauses (thinking pauses, 「那個…」, a counted list) and count how many get cut off mid-thought against the previous install's behavior. Then judge the other direction: does the end of a finished sentence still get answered promptly, or does the extra 200 ms read as a lag? Journal: the session must open with no `session.update rejected; retrying with legacy transcription shape` warning — its absence is the positive signal that the live API accepted the pinned reasoning.effort (the retry drops that field along with the transcription extras). Mitigation if it is rejected: REALTIME_REASONING_EFFORT=off.

items.behavior: Reply length is taught by prompt, not capped: the hardening block's 回答長度 section and the persona's calibration lines say 長度跟著內容走 — a one-line answer where one line suffices, a real explanation or story where the topic deserves it — while cutting filler (repeating the speaker, restating itself, unasked background, reading tool data verbatim, more than one clarifying question at a time) and 「讓我想想」-style preambles, which gpt-realtime-2.x generates by default. REALTIME_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=900 (~40 s of speech) is a runaway-monologue rail only.
items.verification: Subjective, on-robot across a normal session: (1) does a simple question get a short answer, and does 「解釋一下…」 still get a real, willing explanation — i.e. does length track the content rather than a flat rule; (2) no preambles before the substance; (3) no repeating back what the speaker just said, no restating its own previous answer, no unasked background; (4) tool results are stated, not read out verbatim. Journal: `Reply cut off by REALTIME_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (status=incomplete)` must be ABSENT in normal use — if it appears, the rail is too tight (raise REALTIME_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS), not evidence that the robot is verbose. Watch also for `response ended status=... reason=...` INFO lines, the other non-completed statuses.

items.behavior: After the 1200 ms pre-greeting wake check misses (14/14 boots since 2026-08-24 did), a bounded extended window keeps looking for FACE_WAKE_EXTENDED_MS (default 8000, clamp 0–20000, 0 disables) after the greeting is queued, and on a hit injects a context item so Reachy greets the person by name late. It runs once per app start, honors the FACE_AUTO_GREET kill switch, closes silently the moment the user speaks (a context item landing mid-turn could steer the answer), aborts if the session reconnects, and is cancelled-and-awaited at shutdown — recognition never becomes a continuous scan (D-013).

Negative control (nobody in frame at all): the window must end with `Extended wake face check: no recognition in N round(s); window closed.` — proving the bound. Speaking immediately after boot must instead produce no injection at all.

items.behavior: While a person is recognized, memory is scoped to them: `remember` writes the fact into that person's people.v1.json record and returns `scope: person:<name>` (falling back to the global store only if the person store refuses the name), `forget` searches that person's facts before the global ones, and `who_is_this` returns `known_facts` on a recognized answer. deps.current_person is set by the boot wake check, the extended window and every recognized who_is_this, and is cleared PER SESSION (handler init and on reconnect) — deliberately NOT by a non-recognized glance, so a blink or a too_far look mid-conversation cannot drop a valid label.
items.verification: On-robot, one session: get recognized (boot or 「你認得我嗎」), then say a fact about yourself. Journal must show `Tool call: remember person=<name> fact=…` and the tool result must carry `scope: person:<name>`. Negative control in a session where nobody is recognized: the same sentence must log `Tool call: remember fact=…` (global). Persistence: restart the app and boot recognized again — the greeting must weave that fact in (`Startup greeting personalized for <name> with K remembered fact(s).` with K larger than before). Label stickiness: after a who_is_this that comes back too_far or no_face, a further remember must still land person-scoped.
items.evidence: Unit-verified only (person/global scoping, the person->global fallback, forget's person-first search, who_is_this known_facts, and the per-session clear incl. reconnect). DEPLOY DEPENDENCY: people.v1.json lives beside faces.v1.json inside site-packages and is wiped by every reinstall — it must be added to the reachy-deploy backup/restore manifest before the cross-session half of this row can survive a redeploy.
items.next_action: operator on-robot: recognized session -> remember a fact (check scope) -> restart -> recognized boot again and listen for that fact; plus the unrecognized-session global control

items.behavior: remember_face brackets its capture burst (first sample plus up to 2 extras) with a still pose: movement_manager.set_hold_still(True) parks the head at its current pose on a weight-0 anchor, wobbling is disabled, a 0.35 s settle runs before the first frame, and the release happens in a finally so a cancellation cannot leave the robot parked. While held, set_speaking / set_head_tracking update their flags but issue no robot calls (deferred application on release) and a queued move is dropped with `Move dropped during still-pose hold` — the photo wins.
items.verification: On-robot: say 「記住我，我叫X」 while holding still. The head must visibly stop moving for the burst and resume tracking afterwards, and speech-reactive wobble must come back. Journal must show `Tool call: remember_face saved name=X samples=N` with N >= 2 and NO `hold_still: could not …` warning. Then confirm the restore for real: keep talking and moving after the call and check the head follows again. Optional: trigger an emotion during the burst and expect the `Move dropped during still-pose hold` line rather than a moved head.
items.evidence: Unit-verified only (hold/release incl. restore-on-exception and cancellation, deferred mid-hold application, move drop). The 0.35 s settle is a guess that has never met the real head: it is the one number in this row that live use is expected to correct. Known residual (Task 6 review, deferred): stop() can skip stop_head_tracking() if shutdown lands inside a hold after a mid-hold tracking-off toggle, leaving a weight-0 tracker armed.

items.behavior: A verbal enrollment keeps ONE posed JPEG per person (the D-013 amendment of 2026-08-28, operator-directed): once remember_face accepts its first sample, that frame is copied and encoded fire-and-forget through the already-shipped imageio-ffmpeg binary into <instance>/face_snapshots/<record_id>.jpg (q:v 4 ~ quality 85, atomic tmp+rename, overwritten on re-enroll, the subprocess bounded at 10 s and run off the event loop). It can never fail, delay or raise into the enrollment result. Recognition itself stays snapshot-free and no other code path writes an image. The Mac-side import then copies the file over as a display-only photo, so a person imported from a voice enrollment has a face beside their name in the backend UI.
items.verification: On-robot, AFTER the next deploy — nothing backfills anyone enrolled before it, so this needs a FRESH enrollment: say the enrollment phrase, and confirm the tool answers at its usual speed with no snapshot warning in the journal; then over ssh `ls -l <instance>/face_snapshots/` shows exactly one <record_id>.jpg matching the new record, in the low hundreds of KB. On the Mac: run the import and look at the person's photo grid — the picture is there, labelled 'robot snapshot - display only' — and a second import adds no second copy. The robot's recognition samples must be unchanged by any of it.
items.evidence: Unit-verified on both sides. Robot: a decodable JPEG is written, the enrollment result is unaffected when the encoder fails or is missing, the snapshot fires only on a successful enroll, the frame is detached from the camera buffer, and the encode happens after the still-pose hold releases. Backend: one fetch per applied face, stored display-only with no embedding, sha256-deduped, missing file and failed transfer both tolerated, hostile record ids never interpolated. Never run on the robot: the ffmpeg encode of a real HD camera frame is unmeasured (expected ~2.8-4 MB raw frame in, low-hundreds-KB JPEG out), and face_snapshots/ must join the reachy-deploy backup/restore manifest or the first reinstall wipes every picture.

items.behavior: Robot-side writes come back to the Mac on an explicit, previewed import: a face voice-enrolled on the robot arrives as a new backend person (or attaches to an existing unlinked one, with a surfaced conflict when it would collide with a different face id), its embeddings arrive as synthetic photos, person-scoped facts created by voice arrive as facts, and a fact FORGOTTEN by voice is applied as a deletion rather than being silently reverted by the next push. Until the import runs, a push that would overwrite unknown robot content is refused. Merged people stay reachable through the same path: a robot record under a merged-away name, or under a record id the survivor used to carry, resolves onto the survivor via aliases / former_face_ids; a re-enrollment under an alias attaches to the survivor and its fresh record id is remembered rather than importing as a duplicate; and "changed" now means an embedding unknown to ANY stored photo of that person (not merely absent from the projected newest-3), so one import clears the block and the push may legitimately collapse two robot records into the survivor's single projected one. Every face an import applies also best-effort scps face_snapshots/<record_id>.jpg off the robot and stores it as a display-only photo — shown in the UI, never embedded, structurally excluded from the projected sample window, and sha256-deduped so a re-import adds nothing.

On the Mac: GET /api/sync/status shows drift, POST /api/sync/push returns 409 with the diff, GET /api/sync/import previews it, POST applies it -> `Imported N items from the robot with K conflicts.`; the person appears in the UI with a synthetic photo tile and the fact. The push must then succeed and the next push after that be byte-identical. Removal half: with a person who has FEWER than 20 facts on the Mac, say 「忘記…」 person-scoped on the robot, import, and confirm the fact is gone from the Mac store. Merge half: with the two records the robot produced for one person (the 'Linna'/'Lena' mishearing), merge them on the person page — the survivor keeps its name and shows the other as an alias badge — then run import -> push and confirm the robot ends holding ONLY the survivor and that the next GET /api/sync/status diff is empty. Snapshot half is ENROLL-SNAPSHOT's row.

KNOWN HOLE, deliberate: a Mac person with >= 20 facts always projects at exactly 20, so a robot-side removal for them is indistinguishable from cap eviction and the removal is never read back — pick a person under the cap for the removal row. Faces removals are not modelled at all (no robot-side person-deletion tool exists). The merge and snapshot halves are unit-verified only as well: alias-resolved fact matching and attach, a former-id record read as known rather than new, two robot ids mapping to one survivor importing once and then pushing clean, the whole post-merge push cycle, a fact forgotten under a former face id; and for snapshots, one fetch per applied face, sha256 dedupe against an existing real photo's bytes, a missing file and a failed scp both tolerated, and thirteen hostile record ids (separators, spaces, quotes, $, ;, globs) never reaching a remote path. Nothing here has run against the robot.

items.behavior: Going to sleep leaves a callback behind: every person recognized during the app run gets ONE superseding `上次聊天（M月D日）：…` fact summarizing the visit. The visit is the unit — a bounded 40-item transcript tail (`session_transcript`) and the set of every name recognized this run (`recognized_people`) live on ToolDependencies and are deliberately NOT cleared on session reconnect, unlike `current_person`. Both are stamped with time.monotonic() (`recognized_at`, written only through `record_recognition`), because the two spans differ: once tail lines have been evicted, only people last seen at-or-after the oldest surviving line are summarized, so an all-day-awake robot cannot write tonight's topics into this morning's visitor's fact. Talking refreshes the speaker's stamp — current_person, or the SOLE guest when a reconnect has cleared that label (_run_realtime_session clears it on every session and the wake checks are one-shot per handler); with 2+ known and no label, nobody's — so a long visit, reconnects included, never summarizes nobody. Only the accepted user final and the assistant final are recorded (exactly two sites); the party-mode DENIED ambient turn and the solo-barge ROLLED-BACK backchannel are excluded — speech the robot decided was not addressed to it is not conversation. The summarizer runs once at handler shutdown, gated on `deps.sleep_requested` which ONLY the voice go_to_sleep closure sets (settings/backend restarts also reach shutdown() mid-visit), and it runs AFTER on_session_shutdown so the daemon's speaker is already stopped before a call that can take seconds. One gpt-5-mini call (MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_MODEL), MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S 8.0 s clamped 1-30, MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_ENABLED kill switch; every failure logs an exception type and writes nothing. Supersession is by the 上次聊天 prefix alone (no PersonFact schema change): ADD then FORGET, with a FORGET-first branch at the 20-fact cap and whenever an old fact's forget-key is contained in the new one. Being newest-first the fact lands inside the FACE_GREETING_FACTS (6) facts the boot greeting and who_is_this already inject, so the next recognized boot can call back to it with no greeting-code change.
items.verification: On-robot, TWO sessions, AFTER the sixteenth install. Session one: get recognized (boot or 「你認得我嗎」) and talk about something ongoing (an exam, a trip, a song being written), then say 「請進入睡眠模式」. The journal must show `Sleep summary: wrote last-chat fact for 1 person(s).` AFTER the music/session shutdown lines, and over ssh `people.v1.json` must hold exactly ONE fact for that person starting `上次聊天（` with today's date. Session two: boot recognized as the same person — the greeting must reference that thread (「上次你說…後來呢？」) rather than reciting facts, and `Startup greeting personalized for <name> with K remembered fact(s).` must show the callback among the K. Negative control: stop the app from the dashboard instead of by voice — no `Sleep summary:` line, no new fact. Second negative control (visit window, needs the robot left awake): person A is recognized in the morning and talks; hours later, without any restart, person B is recognized and holds a long conversation (past the 40-line tail); on voice sleep the journal must report ONE person summarized and only B may gain a new 上次聊天 fact — A's must be untouched, still carrying its old date. Third session (supersession): repeat session one and confirm the person still has exactly ONE 上次聊天 fact, carrying the new date, with every real fact intact.
items.evidence: Unit-verified only (reachy_companion/tests/test_sleep_summary.py, 31 tests): the prefixed fact is written; a previous 上次聊天 fact is superseded; the same-day substring, case-variant and whitespace-variant collisions all leave exactly one fact — that trio was a PROVEN SILENT DELETE found in review, because forget_person_fact matches on a case-insensitive, whitespace-collapsed SUBSTRING newest-first, so guards keyed on raw text let the post-add forget remove the fact just written; at the 20-fact cap the forget-first branch keeps every real fact; no people or no transcript is a no-op; a client failure, bad JSON and an unlisted name all write nothing; the kill switch is honoured; the visit window is pinned four ways (2026-08-30) — a guest last seen hours before the retained tail is dropped and never even named to the model, one recognized mid-tail is kept, the sole speaker of a long visit is kept because talking refreshes the stamp, and an all-stale roster returns 0 with NO model call at all; the reconnect regression is pinned too — a websocket drop clears current_person and nothing re-sets it, so a single-guest visit that talks 50 more lines afterwards would have summarized NOBODY without the sole-guest fallback, while two known guests with no label refresh nobody; and the handler half is pinned twice — a shutdown WITHOUT sleep_requested writes nothing, and one WITH it summarizes exactly once with its own client and in the order ['music_stop', 'summary'], so the ordering cannot regress silently. BLOCKER: nothing here has run on the robot — this needs the SIXTEENTH INSTALL (the persona half is already live, sha 1ce532f3…, but every code path above rides the next wheel), and then a two-session live test with a real recognized person. RESIDUAL RISK to watch on that run: the summary is a network call inside shutdown, so a daemon that force-kills the app during sleep could race the <=8 s window and leave no fact — the failure is silent by design (no fact, no traceback), so judge it by the missing `Sleep summary:` journal line rather than by an error. SECOND RESIDUAL RISK, unmeasured: gpt-5-mini's real latency against MEMORY_LAST_CHAT_TIMEOUT_S=8.0 s — a reasoning model can spend that whole budget before its first token, and the timeout is a silent zero. Measure it on the FIRST on-robot run (journal time between the sleep lines and `Sleep summary:`); if it times out, raise the knob (clamped 1-30 s) or set the summarizer's reasoning effort low. THIRD RESIDUAL, deliberate: a guest is dropped once 40 transcript lines have elapsed since their last recognition or last heartbeat — WHETHER OR NOT they are still in the room speaking, because the heartbeat follows the current_person label (or the sole guest when a reconnect has cleared it) and there is no diarization; the case that loses a callback is a second guest in an unlabelled multi-person visit.

Prompt-only: no code path changes, because facts have always been free text.

items.behavior: An operator-run pass tidies the Mac people store: companion_backend/scripts/consolidate.py hands each person's whole fact list to the model and stores back a merged, de-contradicted (「以前…，現在…」), usefulness-ranked one. Dry run by default and the printed unified diff IS the write — `after` is normalized and deduped exactly as store.replace_facts will hold it. An answer is validated whole or refused whole, and a refusal costs that person nothing. Writes go through store.replace_facts(..., preserve_updated_at=True), the store's only in-place writer, so a background pass never reshuffles the projection's recency ranking (position matters as much as the timestamp, because that sort is stable); the Mac store stays uncapped and only projection trims to 20. 上次聊天 facts are popped before the prompt, any the model invents is dropped, and only the newest is put back at position 0 — a keep-newest dedupe that HEALS the sync hole where robot-side removal detection is disabled at the 20-fact cap. Because the store lock is process-local, the CLI FAILS CLOSED: it first asks the kernel who holds the port (`lsof -nP -iTCP:8710 -sTCP:LISTEN`, which sees every bind including a LAN one no address list can guess), then probes :8710/api/config on loopback, COMPANION_BACKEND_HOST and the live `tailscale ip -4` (the documented production bind is the tailnet IP), and only a refused connection on every one of them lets the run continue; a missing lsof is not itself a refusal, because the probes are the floor. Exit codes 0 done / 1 refused or failed / 2 no OpenAI client / 3 backend up or unproven. --import-first and --push-after reuse backend/robot.py directly so the whole round trip runs with the backend stopped, in the only safe order; an empty store is never pushed.
items.verification: On the REAL Mac store, with the backend STOPPED. Seed a person with a duplicate pair and a contradiction (e.g. 「想當舞者」 + 「現在是外科醫師」) plus one 上次聊天 fact. Dry run: `../reachy_companion/.venv/bin/python scripts/consolidate.py` prints a unified diff merging the duplicates and folding the contradiction into one 「以前…，現在…」 line, keeps the 上次聊天 fact at the top, exits 0, and `people.json` is byte-identical afterwards. Then `--apply`: the store holds exactly what the dry run printed, and the person's updated_at and position in people.json are unchanged. Guard: start the backend and run again — it must print REFUSED and exit 3, on the TAILNET bind as well as loopback. One-shot flow: with the backend down, `--import-first --apply --push-after` completes import -> consolidate -> push and the robot's people.v1.json reflects the consolidated facts; `--push-after` without `--apply` must be refused.
items.evidence: Unit-verified only (companion_backend/tests/test_consolidate.py 45 tests + the replace_facts tests in tests/test_store.py): the dry run writes not one byte; apply writes through replace_facts with preserve_updated_at; `after` is reported exactly as the store will hold it; a bad payload is refused whole and writes nothing; the model never sees a 上次聊天 fact, one it invents is dropped, an answer that is nothing but invented callbacks is refused, the newest is kept first and older ones deduped even with no model call, and the list is capped at the robot's twenty; test_full_sync_cycle_heals_stale_last_chat pins the whole import -> consolidate -> push cycle healing a stale callback; test_the_last_chat_prefix_matches_the_robot_s_own pins the restated prefix to reachy_companion's own (restated, never imported, because reachy_companion.config runs load_dotenv(override=True) at import time and would rewrite this process's OPENAI_API_KEY); and the guard is pinned on both halves — an answering backend, an unprovable one, the three candidate hosts, stop-at-first-answer, a best-effort tailscale, plus (2026-08-30) a process holding port 8710 refusing the run before ANY HTTP probe is made, a missing lsof falling through to those probes instead of failing closed, and a best-effort lsof reader. BLOCKER: no run against the real store or a real model — every LLM call in the suite is a spy, and the one-shot --import-first/--push-after flow is MONKEYPATCH-VERIFIED ONLY (backend.robot's import/push are stubbed; they have never been driven from this CLI against the robot). Also unmeasured: cost and latency of a pass over all 12 people, and whether gpt-5-mini's merges read acceptably in Taiwan Traditional Chinese.
